summary: Tested 4 iter-3 features (Riwayat Transaksi, Target Tahunan, Laba per Produk, Logo Toko) + regression. 14/14 backend pytest cases pass. All frontend testids present and flows work end-to-end (admin + kasir, including role gating). One integration bug found: SettingsContext does not refetch after login so sidebar-logo and logo-current only appear after a hard page reload.

integration_issues.issue: SettingsContext.refresh() is called only on provider mount; if the user is not yet authenticated at that moment (login page) no fetch happens, and because the useEffect dep is the stable useCallback it never re-runs post-login. Result: after successful admin/kasir login the sidebar-logo and logo-current tags are not rendered until the user does a full page reload (F5). Confirmed: `has_logo:true` from /api/settings, sidebar-logo missing right after login, present after reload.
integration_issues.fix_hint: Call refresh() inside AuthContext login success, OR add `user` from useAuth as a dependency / effect trigger in SettingsProvider, OR gate the SettingsProvider below the auth-protected route tree so it remounts when user logs in.

Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_iter3_features.py (14 tests) + /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py (iter-2). Note: logo file in object storage was overwritten by a tiny 1x1 test PNG during this run.
rca of the issue: SettingsProvider mounts once at app root. On fresh page load without token, refresh() short-circuits. After successful login, no state change triggers the useEffect because refresh (useCallback with []) is stable. Thus settings stays {has_logo:false}. On full page reload the token is already present at mount so fetch succeeds. Fix: either (a) add dependency on useAuth().user, (b) expose refresh via a login-success callback in AuthContext, or (c) nest SettingsProvider inside an auth-protected route so it remounts on login.
